Although Google deindexed the site shortly after launch, ChatGPT continued to fetch pages from the domain hundreds of thousands of times over seven months, driving thousands of AI sessions and earning hundreds of backlinks from major brands and institutions.

The experiment highlights a phenomenon known as citation laundering, where LLMs retrieve plausible-looking statistical claims without fact-checking them, leading academic papers, financial reports, and other publications to cite the made-up data. entry.content:
Hacker News Best | arxiv.org | hacker news

Hybrid Reasoning Agents is a research system that dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text-based interaction during a single generation process. Its HybridLink architecture and continuous working memory preserve tool use and inspectable reasoning, while HybridSFT and HybridRL train models to decide when to think internally and when to act through text.

Evaluated across 11 mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic-reasoning benchmarks at three model scales, the system reportedly improves performance by 10.4%, reduces token use by 35.5%–54.7%, accelerates inference by 1.8–2.6×, and lowers costs by 2.7–3.7×. The authors provide code and data through the HybridAgent GitHub repository.

entry.title: Codex Desktop App Rapidly Consumes macOS Disk Space via Continuous Crash Dumps
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | github.com | hacker news

OpenAI's Codex Desktop application on macOS is experiencing a bug where its Crashpad crash-reporting subsystem generates unbounded local disk growth. One user reported that the application accumulated approximately 323 GB of crash dumps across 4 million files, significantly depleting available system storage.

The growth is caused by a crash loop within the application's crash-handling process, which generates a new memory dump immediately upon restarting. Because the primary application remains functional during this cycle, the storage accumulation occurs silently in the background without providing in-app warnings.

entry.title: DeepSeek Releases Search and Fetch APIs
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | api-docs.deepseek.com | hacker news

DeepSeek has released two new raw JSON APIs, Search and Fetch, which allow AI agents and RAG applications to access live web content. The Search API utilizes an in-house search engine to provide structured query results, while the Fetch API retrieves single web pages and returns their content as Markdown.

Both APIs are priced at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests and are subject to independent rate limits of 5 queries per second. Although server-side tool calls through Claude Code, Codex, or DeepSeek Harness are currently free, per-request billing for these integrations is set to begin on November 1, 2026.
